medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The School of Medicine values diversity of perspectives in medical education and is committed to the recruitment and retention of talented students from underrepresented and disadvantaged backgrounds. Our recruitment efforts provide applicants from all backgrounds information on admissions requirements and preparation for medical school, the selection process, and educational and research opportunities at the School of Medicine. A complete review process is conducted for all applicants, considering each applicant's background and life experiences as context for their academic performance and preparation for medical school and a career in medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence may be required for purposes of academic remediation or may be granted by the Dean for appropriate personal or professional reasons.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Organizations and societies are available for students with varied interests and from all backgrounds. The new Southern Management Corporation Campus Center provides students with a place to meet and relax, providing outstanding cuisine and full athletic facilities, including a swimming pool.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The professional campus is located in downtown Baltimore within easy walking distance of the Hippodrome Theatre, Inner Harbor, Maryland Science Center, National Aquarium and Pier 6 Pavilion. Oriole Park at Camden Yards and M&T Bank Ravens Stadium sit adjacent to campus. Surrounding neighborhoods provide convenient residential spaces, and opportunities for social interaction and entertainment with restaurants, bars, museums, stadiums, and theaters. Bike and running paths connect the city to large nearby parks and green spaces, along with 7 miles of paved waterfront promenade.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Baltimore offers a variety of housing options for University of Maryland, Baltimore (UMB) students, postdocs, faculty, and staff. Whether you want to live close to campus or in another one of Baltimore’s 250 neighborhoods, there’s a community that can meet your needs. With a mix of apartment buildings, row houses, and single-family homes, there are options for different budgets and preferences. The surrounding neighborhood provides more choices for students, with both apartments and individual homes (townhomes) available for rent (average $800-1200/month) or purchase. A shuttle system is available to facilitate transportation throughout the downtown Baltimore area.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Gender and sexual minority students may participate in the student-led LGBTQ Health Interest group which organizes educational and social events for medical students. Additionally, both the UMB campus-wide Queer Student Alliance and the Stonewall Pride affinity group for faculty and staff organize campus events including Coming Out Day and Transgender Day of Remembrance. All campus security are required to undergo safe space training, which is also available to faculty and staff. Educational content for students includes safe space and LGBT health education.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Our Office of Medical Education provides academic support to all students who may benefit, including those with learning differences. The campus Office for Education Support and Disability Services also provides support to any student on the UMB campus who may benefit, coordinating services to assist students with disabilities in obtaining reasonable accommodations through an interactive process involving the student and the school.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The University of Maryland School of Medicine Wellness Committee is comprised of faculty and staff from the Office of Student Affairs and Wellness Representatives from each medical school class. Its purpose is to facilitate and cultivate well-being among our students.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The University of Maryland School of Medicine boasts a collegial atmosphere that fosters scholarship, collaboration, innovation, and inclusivity. Nestled in an urban setting within a small city with unique neighborhoods, students experience a vibrant and fun environment. This dynamic campus culture supports both academic excellence and personal growth.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: There is a dress code. Students are expected to present themselves in a professional manner at all times in congruence with hospital policy dress code.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Two full-time academic advisors are available in the Office of Medical Education who help arrange tutoring and other academic support services.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient exposure begins during the first year in Practice of Medicine and continues longitudinally throughout the preclerkship period, preparing students for ongoing patient exposure in clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Instruction during the pre-clerkship curriculum is a combination of lecture, team-based learning, and self-assessment.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin spring of second year, and continue through fourth year. Two sub-internships are required in fourth year. Students will need transportation for some clerkship assignments.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: This is designed for students from non-traditional backgrounds and provides  guidance on strategic skills for student success with emphasis on anatomy, cell and molecular biology and biochemistry.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance at lectures is not required. However, there is an attendance policy for small group and team-based learning sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The pre-clerkship curriculum consists of integrated basic and clinical sciences covering normal anatomy and physiology alongside pathophysiology by systems, using interdisciplinary teaching by both basic and clinical science faculty in lecture and team-based learning settings. Curricular materials are available online and laptop computers are required. "Practice of Medicine" begins early in the first year and continues throughout the four years, offering instruction in clinical diagnosis, service learning, biomedical ethics, unconscious bias, safe space, and cultural humility education, and other dynamics of patient care. Preclerkship units end during the spring of year 2, allowing for earlier initiation of clinical clerkships and increased flexibility for Step I preparation.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Students are exposed to primary care through the Primary Care Track elective, rotations through pediatric and family medicine, ambulatory experience in all disciplines, and the four week rural experience during the AHEC (Area Health Education centers) elective. There are also individual interest groups for rural medicine, family medicine, internal medicine and pediatrics.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The Office of Student Research (OSR) provides funded and volunteer positions, advice on research careers, and access to both internal and external research programs for high school, college, and medical students.  The areas of research that students are involved in span the broadest definitions of behavioral and biomedical research conducted by the faculty using established and "cutting-edge" techniques to unravel research questions.  These have included, but are not limited to: genetics and genomic medicine, cardiovascular and pulmonary disease, endocrinologic disorders, environmental health, epidemiology, infectious diseases, immunology, molecular biology, neuroscience, oncology, toxicology and virology.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service learning is a required component of the Practice of Medicine course (all students) and the Medical Spanish elective.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: A scholarly project is required of all medical students.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: University of Maryland Medical Center and Baltimore VA Medical Center are major tertiary care centers. Students also rotate through a variety of community-based hospitals in the Baltimore area.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: The grading system is a tiered pass/fail system (Honors/HP/P/F) and is used for both pre-clerkship and clerkship evaluations.
medSchoolCurriculum.languageInstructions: English, except for the Medical Spanish course that is taught in Spanish.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Organized in 1807, The University of Maryland School of Medicine is the nation's oldest public medical college. The first class was graduated in 1810. The medical school was among the first to erect its own hospital for clinical instruction.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: We pursue excellence across biomedical research, education, and patient care to advance health equity and wellness for people in Baltimore, the State of Maryland, and around the world. Together, we work to solve generational health challenges and make lasting contributions to the betterment of our diverse and interconnected communities.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The University of Maryland B.S.-M.D. program prepares highly motivated undergraduate students majoring in engineering or data science fields to excel in medical school. BS-MD students participate in structured service and clinical activities, along with medically related research with their cohort, which will cultivate a sense of service, community, and innovation in the students. Students apply during their first year at University of Maryland College Park.  Eligible students are majoring in Engineering, Computer Science, or Mathematics.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: When available, a composite pre-medical advisory committee letter is strongly preferred. Similarly, if the pre-medical advisory committee does not provide a letter but does prepare a packet, then a packet prepared by this committee is strongly preferred in order to be most competitive for an interview.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: If a pre-medical advisory committee letter is not available, a minimum of three letters are required. Included in these three letters, we require at least 1 letter from a science professor and 1 letter from a non-science professor, from whom the applicant has taken courses. Beyond these 3 letters, additional letters can come from employers, shadowed physicians, service activity supervisors, and research investigators with whom the applicant has worked.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Our interview day format will be remote in order to keep our applicants and SOM community safe and to ensure equity in the admissions process. Applicants will receive a presentation from the Office of Financial Aid, an information session conducted by the Associate Dean or Assistant Dean for Admissions, and will meet current students during the lunch and a Q&A. We will host in-person campus visits for the 2026 cycle for accepted students, and we will welcome accepted students to our campus in the late winter of 2027 for a Second Look visit.  

For more information: https://www.medschool.umaryland.edu/admissions/Your-Path-to-Medical-School/ (see Interview Day section)
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two interviews are conducted in a one-on-one format by trained faculty and student interviewers. Interviews usually last about 45 minutes.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: We plan to continue remote interviews for the 2027 cycle.

medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores are reviewed as a single factor in a multifactorial holistic review process.  The MCAT score is also placed into context of the applicant's background and life experiences.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: With respect to the score itself, scores over 502 are generally viewed as a "Pass". The MCAT score is also placed into context of the applicant's background and life experiences.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: There is no clear-cut minimum undergraduate GPA required for higher education coursework to be considered. Each application is review holistically, taking into consideration the applicant's background and life experiences. Applicants with a BCPM GPA <3.2 are considered to be at high risk for failing academically.  This can be overcome by an excellent post-bacc or graduate school GPA.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: There is no clear-cut minimum undergraduate GPA required for higher education coursework to be considered. Each application is review holistically, taking into consideration the applicant's background and life experiences. Applicants with a BCPM GPA <3.2 are considered to be at high risk for failing academically.  This can be overcome by an excellent post-bacc or graduate school GPA.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept coursework from community colleges including for pre-requisites.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Any of this information can be uploaded through the application portal.  Consider submitting an update for new publications or if your plans during the application year change significantly in a way that impacts your interest in medicine (i.e. additional shadowing, service, clinical activities, etc.)
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The University of Maryland School of Medicine is committed to the full and equitable inclusion and support of qualified learners with disabilities. It is the responsibility of the faculty to select matriculants who are best qualified to successfully complete the required training and develop into skilled, effective, and compassionate physicians that will fulfill the mission of the School. Applicants and matriculated students will be judged not only on their scholastic achievement and abilities, but also on their intellectual, physical, emotional, and ethical capacities to meet the essential requirements of the school’s curriculum. The School of Medicine will consider for admission those individuals who possess the ability to successfully complete the academically rigorous curriculum and the personal characteristics embodied by exemplary physicians. These are guided by the AAMC Core Competencies for Entering Medical Students.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: We encourage applicants to narrow down to 3 acceptances by April 15th, as per the AAMC Choose Your Medical School tool protocols.
Applicants must personally notify each institution directly that they are withdrawing their acceptance, in addition to making this selection on the Choose Your Medical School page.

Applicants with more than one acceptance must withdraw from all but their first choice of medical school by April 30th. If you are choosing our medical school, please select "Commit to Enroll" by April 30, 2025. Applicants holding acceptances to other medical schools beyond April 30th, may have their offer of acceptance withdrawn.

Applicants who have selected "Commit to Enroll" for our school who are also holding waitlist spots at other institutions must withdraw from all other waitlists by June 1st. Applicants who have not withdrawn from other waitlist spots may have their acceptance offer to our institution rescinded.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are informed that they are ranked in the upper or lower half of the Waitlist. Acceptances are offered as seats become available.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Applicants with a Bachelor's degree are given strong preference in the selection process. Credit hours must have been earned at an accredited institution of postsecondary education in the United States or Canada as defined by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation. Community college credit is acceptable, but the Committee on Admissions prefers that the bulk of the required and recommended courses be taken at a four year institution. In light of the COVD-19 crisis we will accept online course credit for prerequisite courses for the 2020 spring, summer, and fall semesters, as well as the spring 2021 semester.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: It is preferred that the pre-requisite coursework be taken within five years of the date of the application to medical school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Admission to the medical school is not restricted to Maryland residents. All AMCAS applicants are invited to submit a  secondary application. Selection of students is based on careful appraisal of each applicant's academic achievement and MCAT scores and their maturity, character and motivation for a career in medicine as demonstrated in the Personal Comments, extracurricular activities, letters of recommendation and interview evaluations. Invitations to interview  are made at the discretion of the Committee on Admissions. The University of Maryland School of Medicine does not discriminate in its selection process on the basis of race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, protected veteran's status, physical or mental disability, or age.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants are expected to gain exposure to clinical medicine, including shadowing, scribing, or translating experiences that provide applicants insight into the physician-patient relationship and into the realities of a career in medicine. There is no set number of hours required.
